cards.title: Design for Breakdowns
cards.body: Intentionally design how the idea could go wrong. Focus on errors, misunderstandings, misuse, and abandonment.

cards.title: Make It Strange
cards.body: Invert a familiar assumption, role, rule, or sequence. What becomes possible when the obvious version is removed?

cards.title: Borrow From Elsewhere
cards.body: Find a useful pattern in another discipline, culture, system, or living thing. Translate its logic into this situation.

cards.title: Argue the Opposite
cards.body: Make the strongest case for the opposite of your current direction. What does this reveal?

cards.title: Change the Scale
cards.body: Explore the opportunity at a radically different size: tiny enough to hold or large enough to reshape a system.

cards.title: Think in Relationships
cards.body: Focus less on individual objects and more on the relationships between people, places, tools, and events.

cards.title: Remove the Obvious
cards.body: Take away the feature, behaviour, resource, or assumption that currently feels most essential.

cards.title: Follow the Consequence
cards.body: Imagine your current idea becomes successful. What second- and third-order effects follow?

cards.title: Find the Hidden Rule
cards.body: Identify an unspoken rule shaping the situation. What happens when you challenge, reverse, or expose it?

cards.title: Switch the Subject
cards.body: Reconsider the situation from the perspective of someone or something usually treated as secondary.

cards.title: Look for the Tension
cards.body: Find two values, needs, or desires that appear to conflict. What might emerge by designing for both?

cards.title: Start With the Feeling
cards.body: Begin with a desired emotional state rather than a function or feature. What would create that feeling?

cards.title: Make It Temporary
cards.body: Imagine the idea only exists for one day, one hour, or one interaction. What changes?

cards.title: Find the Metaphor
cards.body: Describe the opportunity as a physical object, landscape, ritual, creature, or weather system. What does the metaphor suggest?

cards.title: Ask What Is Missing
cards.body: Look at the current situation and identify the absence, silence, gap, or unrepresented experience.

cards.title: Make a Rough Version
cards.body: Turn the thought into something visible, audible, tangible, or walkable in ten minutes.

cards.title: Act It Out
cards.body: Perform what happens before, during, and after the moment you are exploring.

cards.title: Build With Constraints
cards.body: Make a version using only the materials, time, tools, or people immediately available.

cards.title: Show the First Five Minutes
cards.body: Prototype only the beginning. What does someone encounter, do, notice, or feel first?

cards.title: Make Two Bad Versions
cards.body: Create two deliberately flawed versions. Notice what each bad version teaches you.

cards.title: Sequence the Experience
cards.body: Arrange the idea as a series of moments. What must happen first, next, and last?

cards.title: Prototype the Exception
cards.body: Make a version for an unusual, difficult, or unexpected situation.

cards.title: Make It Without Explaining
cards.body: Express the idea through a sketch, gesture, object, or sequence without using explanatory language.

cards.title: Swap the Materials
cards.body: Build the idea using an unexpected material or medium. What does the material make you notice?

cards.title: Design the Handoff
cards.body: Prototype what happens when responsibility, information, or an object moves from one person to another.

cards.title: Make the Invisible Visible
cards.body: Create a model of something usually hidden: waiting, uncertainty, trust, effort, memory, or decision-making.

cards.title: Try It Backwards
cards.body: Perform or prototype the experience in reverse order. What does the reversal reveal?

cards.title: Create a Rule
cards.body: Invent one simple rule that shapes the activity or experience. See what it enables and prevents.

cards.title: Make It Social
cards.body: Turn the idea into something that requires interaction between at least two people.

cards.title: Prototype the Ending
cards.body: Start with the final moment. What does completion, departure, recovery, or continuation look like?

cards.title: Look at the Edge
cards.body: Focus on the person, condition, or context furthest from the assumed centre.

cards.title: Find the Friction
cards.body: Notice where effort, confusion, waiting, silence, or repetition gathers.

cards.title: Listen for the Unsaid
cards.body: Identify what is assumed, avoided, normalised, or left unspoken.

cards.title: Follow the Attention
cards.body: Observe what people look at, ignore, return to, or struggle to find.

cards.title: Notice the Workaround
cards.body: Find where people invent their own solutions. What does the workaround reveal?

cards.title: Track the Energy
cards.body: Notice when energy rises, drops, concentrates, or disperses across the situation.

cards.title: Look for the Threshold
cards.body: Find the moment where someone enters, exits, commits, hesitates, or changes their mind.

cards.title: Observe the Waiting
cards.body: Pay attention to what happens during pauses, delays, queues, and moments of uncertainty.

cards.title: Find the Ritual
cards.body: Identify a repeated behaviour that gives the situation rhythm, meaning, or belonging.

cards.title: Notice What Gets Counted
cards.body: What is measured, recorded, rewarded, or prioritised? What remains invisible?

cards.title: Map the Dependencies
cards.body: Notice what relies on what, and where one small change creates a larger effect.

cards.title: Look for the Mismatch
cards.body: Find where the stated intention differs from the lived experience.

cards.title: Observe the Boundary
cards.body: Identify who or what is included, excluded, protected, delayed, or asked to adapt.

cards.title: Follow the Object
cards.body: Choose one object, message, or piece of information and trace its journey.

cards.title: Notice the Mood
cards.body: Describe the atmosphere of the situation without explaining its cause. What shapes that mood?

cards.title: Design for Misuse
cards.body: Imagine the idea is misunderstood, repurposed, or used in an unintended way.

cards.title: Stress the System
cards.body: Push the idea until it meets its limits: more people, less time, higher stakes, or a new setting.

cards.title: Remove a Resource
cards.body: Take away a tool, feature, habit, permission, or material that currently feels essential.

cards.title: Make It Uncomfortable
cards.body: Introduce a productive discomfort. What might people need to confront, question, or renegotiate?

cards.title: Design for Rejection
cards.body: Imagine someone refuses, ignores, or abandons the idea. How does the experience respond?

cards.title: Question the Beneficiary
cards.body: Ask who benefits most from the current direction and who might carry the cost.

cards.title: Make It Too Much
cards.body: Exaggerate the idea until it becomes excessive. What useful quality becomes visible?

cards.title: Make It Too Little
cards.body: Reduce the idea to its smallest possible expression. What remains essential?

cards.title: Expose the Trade-Off
cards.body: Identify what the idea improves and what it might worsen.

cards.title: Design for Conflict
cards.body: Imagine people with incompatible needs using the same system or experience.

cards.title: Reverse the Priority
cards.body: Take the least important consideration and make it the main design priority.

cards.title: Test the Assumption
cards.body: Name the assumption your idea depends on most. What happens if it is false?

cards.title: Design for Recovery
cards.body: Focus on what happens after a mistake, failure, misunderstanding, or breakdown.

cards.title: Give It to the Opponent
cards.body: Imagine the idea is designed by someone who strongly disagrees with your current values.

cards.title: Ask Who Pays
cards.body: Consider who contributes time, effort, attention, risk, money, or emotional labour.

cards.title: Jump Ten Years
cards.body: Imagine the opportunity has become ordinary ten years from now. What does a normal day look like?

cards.title: What If It Were a Ritual?
cards.body: Imagine the idea as something repeated over time. What would it mean to participate?

cards.title: Imagine the Ideal Version
cards.body: Remove practical limitations temporarily. What would the most generous version of this opportunity offer?

cards.title: Imagine the Opposite Future
cards.body: Picture a future where the current problem has intensified rather than improved.

cards.title: Give It a Character
cards.body: Imagine the idea has a personality, voice, habits, and preferences. How would it behave?

cards.title: Change the World Around It
cards.body: Keep the idea but alter the surrounding society, technology, climate, culture, or economy.

cards.title: Imagine It as a Place
cards.body: What kind of place would this idea create? Describe its layout, atmosphere, boundaries, and inhabitants.

cards.title: Start With a Memory
cards.body: Imagine someone looking back on this experience years later. What do they remember?

cards.title: Make It Mythic
cards.body: Turn the opportunity into a myth, fable, legend, or origin story. What deeper meaning appears?

cards.title: Imagine It Belongs to Everyone
cards.body: What would change if the idea were collectively owned, shaped, and maintained?

cards.title: Imagine It Belongs to No One
cards.body: What happens when responsibility is distributed, ambiguous, or absent?

cards.title: Create an Alternate Normal
cards.body: Imagine a world where the current assumptions have never existed. What would feel ordinary there?

cards.title: Design the Unlikely Guest
cards.body: Imagine an unexpected person, species, object, or force entering the situation.

cards.title: Imagine the Quiet Version
cards.body: Remove spectacle, urgency, and performance. What remains when the idea becomes quiet and everyday?

cards.title: Write the Future Artifact
cards.body: Imagine finding an object, instruction, message, or photograph from the future that embodies this possibility.
